clue.text: Yank calls on way to use influence

indicators.note: calls are placed on, i.e. after, the way in the answer

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
rings means telephone calls

explanation.surface: An American shouting down the road to get his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull strings is an idiom for using personal connections to get something done.

clue.text: Sign mostly put on a road

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to place is to put

explanation.surface: A sign is mostly installed on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter from PLACE, leaving PLAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a printed notice or poster displayed publicly.

clue.text: Wants to be slow, cycling

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter goes round to the back of the word

parts.note: to slack is to be slow or idle

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to take it easy on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the S of SLACK from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: If something lacks an item it is short of it, which is what wants means.

clue.text: Talk at length about scourge and spend extravagantly

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to spout is to talk at length pompously
to lash is to whip, or scourge

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth on punishment and then going on a spending spree.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out is an idiom for spending money freely on a treat.

clue.text: In lecture, a reason for being stern

indicators.note: In means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A lecturer giving reasons for being strict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' as strict misleads; it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern of a ship is its rear part.

clue.text: One refuses any different speaker

indicators.note: different means the letters are put in another order

parts.note: a sayer is one who says, a speaker

explanation.surface: Someone declines whatever new spokesperson is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A naysayer is someone who habitually objects or says no.

clue.text: Dross incorporating new means of expression

indicators.note: incorporating means taking another piece inside

parts.note: slag is the waste dross from smelting

explanation.surface: Rubbish containing a novel way of expressing oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary, a casual way of expressing oneself.

clue.text: Nag's expression of annoyance about broken pen

indicators.note: about means wrapping around another piece

parts.note: heck is a mild exclamation of annoyance

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A horse snorts in irritation over a broken pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a horse, but it is the verb; 'broken' scrambles the pen and 'about' wraps the exclamation round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To henpeck is to nag constantly, especially a spouse.

clue.text: Bug woman and attempt to stifle resistance

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: to stifle means to smother by enclosing another piece

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A woman tries to suppress opposition from an annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like a verb meaning annoy; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybird, called a ladybug in America, is a small spotted beetle, loosely a bug.

clue.text: Name adopted by racially abused subordinate

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by the other piece
abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A junior employee renamed after suffering racial abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges RACIALLY into ACILLARY, which takes N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancillary means secondary or supporting, providing help to a main thing.

clue.text: American has answer during short encore

indicators.note: during means placed within another piece

parts.note: a short is a measure of spirits, such as gin

explanation.surface: An American gives a brief answer while calling for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a small serving of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is a call for a repeat performance, once more.

clue.text: Help musician losing lead

indicators.note: losing lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a bassist is a musician playing bass

explanation.surface: A band needs help after losing its lead player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests a lead singer, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to give support or aid.

clue.text: Good progress needed in shifting early architectural feature

indicators.note: needed in means put within the other piece
shifting means the letters move into a new arrangement

parts.note: to go is to proceed or progress

explanation.surface: Good progress needed early on an architectural project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' looks like timing but is anagram fodder for 'shifting'; 'needed in' puts the progress inside those shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved grotesque waterspout on a building, a decorative architectural element.

clue.text: Tediously continue racing yacht

definitions.meaning: to ... is to go on for too long
a classic keelboat used in racing

explanation.surface: A racing yacht that keeps going and going.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag on is an idiom for lasting tediously; Dragon is an Olympic racing yacht class.

clue.text: Porter, say, must keep a dray and available fare

indicators.note: must keep means holding other pieces inside

parts.note: porter is a type of dark beer, an example of ale
a dray is a cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A porter loads a brewer's dray with food for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like someone who carries things; it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A la carte means dishes ordered individually from the menu, each priced separately.

clue.text: Decent type attached to leftie sort of university

indicators.note: attached to means the next piece is joined on to this one

parts.note: a red is a left-wing person
a brick is a reliable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: A decent left-winger linked to a kind of university.
explanation.walkthrough: A redbrick is one of the British universities founded in the late 1800s and early 1900s in industrial cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbrick describes a class of British universities, contrasted with Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: People who are barred want to be amongst celebs of the second water

indicators.note: to be amongst means placed in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: B-list celebrities are second-rank; 'of the second water' means second-rate
to lack is to want

explanation.surface: Banned people longing to mingle with second-rate celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacklist is a register of people excluded or banned.

clue.text: Cardinal may see fortune wasted taking drug

indicators.note: taking means taking in another piece
wasted means ruined, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A churchman squanders a fortune on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a prelate; it is a cardinal number. 'wasted' turns FORTUNE into FOURTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fourteen is a cardinal number, one used for counting.

clue.text: Response from soldiers with instruction to shoot

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a film director calls action to start shooting

explanation.surface: Soldiers react when ordered to fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests firing guns; it is filming a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a reply or response to something.

clue.text: Minister's place has lines under right-hand page

indicators.note: under means placed beneath the other piece in this down answer

parts.note: the recto is the right-hand page of a book
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A minister's study has lines written beneath the right page.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a rector, a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Look grand with leading lady

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
and means with, joining two things
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A star looks splendid alongside the leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Gander is informal British usage for a look, as in take a gander.

clue.text: Pay attention to detail

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to heed it
a ... is a particular point, as in 'in every ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Respect means to heed or regard, and also a specific aspect or detail.

clue.text: Outcries about student affairs

parts.note: C is circa, about
L is a learner, a student driver
amours are love affairs

explanation.surface: Protests over students' love lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamours are loud protests or noisy demands.

clue.text: What might measure the spirit of a viewer

definitions.meaning: a device on a bottle in a British pub dispensing a fixed measure of spirits
relating to the eye, of one who views

explanation.surface: Something that gauges the mood of a spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests mood or soul; it is liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is a pub spirit measure, and as an adjective it relates to sight.

clue.text: They may be under your feet when shifting fish

definitions.text: They may be under your feet when shifting
definitions.meaning: boots with blades or wheels worn to move along
the skate is a flat fish related to the ray

explanation.surface: Fish that get under your feet as they swim about.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates are footwear for gliding on ice or wheels, and also flat, rayed fish.

clue.text: Outline suspicion

definitions.meaning: to draw the outline of something
a slight hint or suspicion, as of a flavour

explanation.definitionFit: Trace means copy an outline, and also a tiny hint or amount.

clue.text: Transport arm of the military on top of tactics

indicators.note: on means placed above the next piece in this down answer

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is an arm of the armed forces

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The air force handles transport as well as tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat floating structure used to carry people or goods.

clue.text: Group desire to leave courgette stewing

indicators.note: stewing means cooked up, so the remaining letters are mixed
to leave means these letters are taken out

parts.note: an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A band wishes to quit stewing vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes URGE from COURGETTE, leaving COTTE; 'stewing' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially musicians.

clue.text: Get rid of poor read that is about queen, perhaps

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so these letters are jumbled
about means going around the next piece

parts.note: IE is id est, that is
a queen is a female cat

explanation.surface: A bad reading about the monarch is struck out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges READ into ERAD. 'queen' suggests royalty; it is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy or remove completely.

clue.text: Voter — one that tweets university in agreement

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: consent is agreement
a tit is a small songbird, which tweets

explanation.surface: A voter who posts on social media from campus, in accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweets' suggests social media posts; it is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a member of an electorate represented by an MP.
